findings.state: Recent activity panel footer, on every default screen, whenever a watched account has had no new signal and no email or call from the user for 5 days or more. Walkthrough: 'NO RECENT RESPONSE · SIETE FOODS · 48D' (SMB book, corpus-smb/dashboard.txt) and 'NO RECENT RESPONSE · DAYFORCE · 33D' (enterprise book).
findings.problem: The label says a buyer has not responded. The number does not measure responses. readStillQuiet (src/lib/edge/edge-data.ts:296-342) takes the later of the account's newest signal date and the user's last email or call to it, and counts days since; it never reads a reply. I ran it: an account that replied yesterday to a message sent 10 days ago is still returned as 10 days; an account that was never contacted and whose newest signal is 33 days old is returned as 33 days; a LinkedIn action yesterday does not reset it. In both demo books the account named is a closed-won customer with no outreach recorded (js/demo-seed-data-smb.js:246 Siete Foods, js/demo-seed-data-ent.js:412 Dayforce), so the first thing a tester reads in this footer is that a customer has not responded, when nothing was sent. A first-time user would chase a reply that was never owed. The unit is also the compressed 'd' the approved replacement had expanded to 'days'.
findings.governing: ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/05_COPY_IMPLEMENTATION_MANIFEST_BATCH_01.json exact_replacements[6] ('STILL QUIET · DAYFORCE · 33D' → 'DAYFORCE · NO RECORDED RESPONSE FOR 33 DAYS'); COPY_STANDARD.md §21 Claims discipline ('If the product knows only that there has been no logged activity, say that'); AUDIT_BRIEF §5 'copy that now claims something the code does not do'. The approved replacement assumed the number measured responses; the code shows it does not, so the wording has to follow the code.
findings.proposed:
Keep the approved structure and name what is measured. Replace lines 297-300 with:
{read.stillQuiet.name} · {t("no new signal or outreach for", { class: "body" })} {read.stillQuiet.days} {t("days")}
— renders 'DAYFORCE · NO NEW SIGNAL OR OUTREACH FOR 33 DAYS'. Update the file comment at lines 23-24 ('accounts without a recent response') to match. OWNER DECISION: if the line is meant to report buyer silence, readStillQuiet has to change: start the count at the user's last outreach, stop it at a recorded reply (outcomeDate on a touch marked replied or referred), count LinkedIn actions as outreach, and leave out accounts whose only deal is closed-won. That changes which account is shown.

findings.state: Recent activity panel, the line shown on a day with no activity, when the last recorded activity was two calendar days ago but less than 48 hours ago (for example Wednesday 9:00 AM, last activity Monday 2:00 PM), and for anything older.
findings.current: No activity recorded today yet. The last recorded activity was yesterday ago at 2:00 PM. / No activity recorded today yet. The last recorded activity was 3d ago at 4:12 PM.
findings.problem: quietLine builds the day word as ageLabel(...) + ' ago' (lines 376-378). ageLabel returns the word 'yesterday' for anything 24 to 48 hours old, so the sentence reads 'yesterday ago' and names the wrong day (the activity was two days earlier). Both sentences above are the actual output of the function (run with now = Wed 09:00; last = Mon 14:00 and last = Sat 16:12). For older activity the sentence puts the compact stamp '3d' inside prose. This is the only sentence the panel shows on a day with no activity, so it is the first thing a returning user reads.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (AUDIT_BRIEF §5 dimension 9, elliptical syntax); COPY_STANDARD.md §19 (explanations use complete propositions; compact stamps are for labels).
findings.proposed: In quietLine stop reusing ageLabel. After the wasYesterday check compute whole calendar days: const days = Math.round((midnight(now) - new Date(when.getFullYear(), when.getMonth(), when.getDate()).getTime()) / 86_400_000); const dayWord = wasYesterday ? t("yesterday") : `${days} ${t("days ago")}`; — renders 'No activity recorded today. The last recorded activity was 2 days ago at 2:00 PM.' Drop 'yet' from the first clause ('No activity recorded today.'); nothing is lost.
testsAffected: src/lib/edge/edge-data.test.ts ('the dead-morning line is honest, never fake-busy' asserts the line contains 'No activity recorded today yet' and 'yesterday')

findings.state: Every default screen, keyboard or screen-reader use, in both the shown and the hidden state of the Recent activity panel.
findings.current: <button class="ledge-strip" aria-label="Recent activity is hidden — click to show"> is always in the page (lines 308-317), and <aside class="ledge-rail" aria-label="Recent activity"> with its 'Hide' button is always in the page (lines 254-306).
findings.problem: Both controls are always rendered and only CSS changes. edge.css:37-40 moves the hidden rail off screen with transform and pointer-events; edge.css:301-319 gives the strip opacity 0 and pointer-events none while the panel is showing. Neither removes the element from the tab order or from assistive technology. While the panel is showing, a keyboard user tabs to an invisible button that a screen reader announces as 'Recent activity is hidden — click to show' (the opposite of the truth), and pressing it does nothing because turnEdgeOn returns early. While the panel is hidden, the off-screen 'Hide' button and the whole list are still focusable and read aloud. The 'Hide' button's own accessible name is just 'Hide'; 'Hide recent activity' exists only as a title.
findings.governing: AUDIT_BRIEF §5 (accessible names in every state) and category A11Y; ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/15_HIGH_SEVERITY_INTERACTION_PATCH.md row 'THE LIVE EDGE IS OFF — CLICK TO TURN ON' → 'RECENT ACTIVITY IS HIDDEN — CLICK TO SHOW' (the wording is implemented; the state it is announced in is wrong).
findings.proposed: Keep both elements for the animation and gate them by state. On the aside add aria-hidden={state === "off"} and inert={state === "off"}. On the strip button add tabIndex={state === "off" ? 0 : -1} and aria-hidden={state !== "off"}. On the Hide button add aria-label={t("Hide recent activity", { class: "body" })}. No visible change.

findings.state: Recent activity panel on any page other than Outbound Studio, for a signed-in workspace that uses the BCC address to capture sent email (Settings, 'Counting your work automatically').
findings.current: 'messages & calls — logged or captured' under the day's count; the count and the 'you' lines are read from localStorage only (edge-data.ts:136-158, 183-252), and loadCloudEvents (LiveEdge.tsx:58-97) reads observations and captured_meetings but not captured email.
findings.problem: 'Captured' tells the user that automatically captured email is in this count. A BCC-captured send is written by supabase/functions/inbound-email/index.ts:148-158 to the cloud table `sequences`. The panel counts from the localStorage key gtmos_outbound_touches, and the only writer of that key is Outbound Studio's own save effect (src/outbound-studio/state.ts:275, fed by src/outbound-studio/lib/cloud-persistence.ts:60-82 when that page boots). So a captured email is not counted, and no 'Outreach recorded for …' line appears, on the Dashboard or any other page until the user opens Outbound Studio on that device. The demo shows the opposite: a 'Sent email recorded for sofia@notion.so.' line arrives live on whatever page is open (demo-stream.ts:128). The Quota Workback pace count (src/quota-workback/v4/lib/pace.ts:70) reads the same key and has the same gap.
findings.governing: COPY_STANDARD.md §21 Claims discipline; AUDIT_BRIEF §5 Function ('copy that now claims something the code does not do'); ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/11_AI_PROMPT_AND_GENERATOR_REWRITE_SPEC.md (examples and demo content must not show more than the product produces).
findings.proposed: In loadCloudEvents (LiveEdge.tsx:58-97) also read the workspace's recent outbound rows: data.sequences.list({ where: { sequence_key: "outbound" }, limit: 50 }), keep rows created inside WIRE_WINDOW_MS, emit { id: `touch:${row.id}`, who: "you", text: 'Outreach recorded for {account}.' } (mergeEvents already drops an id that the local list holds), and add the rows dated today that are not in the local list to the day's count. If that is not done in this pass, change line 272 to 'messages & calls recorded on this device' so the label matches what is counted. I read this path and did not run it against a live workspace.

findings.state: Workspace map panel, first column heading, directly under the filter field. Walkthrough: 'ENTER Welcome … Onboarding … Dashboard'.
findings.problem: The other five column headings name a kind of sales work (Strategy, Find & watch, Work the account, Advance the deal, Diagnose · hand off). 'ENTER' in small capitals directly under a text field reads as the Enter key, and as a heading it only makes sense if the app is pictured as a place to walk into. The three pages under it are where a user starts.
findings.governing: comprehension principle; COPY_STANDARD.md §12 (navigation labels name destinations) and §3 'room' (do not make the reader learn the app-as-a-place picture).

findings.state: Workspace map panel: the filter field placeholder, the fallback sub-line (line 184), and the related-activity card footer (src/lib/follow/FollowPeek.tsx:183).
findings.current: …or start typing a workspace / All workspaces in sales-process order / Recorded context remains available in each related workspace.
findings.problem: 'Workspace' means the user's whole account everywhere else on these screens ('WORKSPACE MAP' two lines above, 'See related activity across the workspace' in the same card, 'Download my workspace' in Settings). Here the same word means one page of it, so 'All workspaces' and 'each related workspace' read as if the user had several workspaces. The jump palette and the help button already call these 'pages' ('Jump to a page…', 'What is this page for?'). 'Recommended next workspace:' (GroundLine.tsx:189) carries the same double meaning but is the approved replacement verbatim, so I list it under retained and raise it as an owner decision.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (consistent terms); docs/language-remediation-2026/19_ROOM_WORD_AUDIT.md ('say page when it means the screen you're on or the one you go to'); COPY_STANDARD.md §2.
findings.proposed: GroundLine.tsx:198 '…or type a page name'. GroundLine.tsx:184 'All pages in sales-process order'. FollowPeek.tsx:183 'Recorded context remains available on each related page.' OWNER DECISION: change the approved 'Recommended next workspace:' to 'Recommended next page:' so one panel does not use the word two ways.
